sentences: A seeded extractor combines a weak random source with a short independent uniform seed to produce nearly uniform output.
The saved question seeks logarithmic seed length together with constant total entropy loss.
Entropy loss measures how much usable randomness disappears during purification rather than how long the original source is.
Keeping that loss constant would make extraction nearly information-efficient while requiring only a small amount of initially perfect randomness.
The historical note omits the error regime and total-loss convention, so those parameters must be restored before comparing the target with known extractor bounds.
